root_cause.text: In `drivers/net/tun.c::tun_xdp_one()`, the short-frame check returned `-EINVAL` without releasing the page allocated by `vhost_net_build_xdp()`, and because `tun_sendmsg()` ignored that error and still reported success, `vhost_tx_batch()` never freed the page-frag, causing a per-packet memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `put_page(virt_to_head_page(xdp->data));` inside `if (unlikely(datasize < ETH_HLEN))` before `return -EINVAL;`, and the CVE notes that `tun_xdp_one()` previously rejected frames shorter than `ETH_HLEN` “without freeing the page,” while `tun_sendmsg()` “discards that -EINVAL and still returns total_len,” letting `vhost_tx_batch()` take the success path and leak one page-frag chunk per short frame.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a page reference leak by releasing the XDP data page before returning on undersized packets.
intent_record.what: The error path in tun_xdp_one() was expanded from a single return statement to a block that first calls put_page(virt_to_head_page(xdp->data)) when datasize < ETH_HLEN, then returns -EINVAL.
intent_record.how: When the received XDP frame is too short to contain an Ethernet header, the code now releases the page backing xdp->data before aborting, preventing a page reference leak on this early-exit path.

commit 049584807f1d797fc3078b68035450a9769eb5c3
Author: Dongli Zhang <dongli.zhang@oracle.com>
Date:   Wed Jul 24 10:04:52 2024 -0700

    tun: add missing verification for short frame
    
    The cited commit missed to check against the validity of the frame length
    in the tun_xdp_one() path, which could cause a corrupted skb to be sent
    downstack. Even before the skb is transmitted, the
    tun_xdp_one-->eth_type_trans() may access the Ethernet header although it
    can be less than ET
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the new guard added at the start of `tun_xdp_one()`: `if (unlikely(datasize < ETH_HLEN)) return -EINVAL;`. The root cause was that short frames were not verified before the XDP path could process them, leading to a corrupted skb / short-frame handling bug. Here, the function already contains the fix by explicitly rejecting frames shorter than the Ethernet header size. Because the vulnerable construct is the absence of this check, and this code now has the check, `has_bug` is false and `is_fixed` is true.
